clue.text: Seafood that's dead? Then transport to main ship!

parts.note: ex means former, no longer living or in office
a clam is a shellfish eaten as seafood

indicators.note: to transport is to carry away, so these letters are carried into a new arrangement

parts.note: Noah's ark was a ship

explanation.surface: An excited instruction: a dead clam, then off by boat to the mother ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafood that's dead' is a clam that is ex. 'transport' reworks TO MAIN into ATIONM. The definition is the closing punctuation itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol at the end of the clue is the punctuation that marks an exclamation.

clue.text: As one heads for Mount Everest when climbing, cold as Skegness?

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads the letters upwards, so backwards
the heads of words are their first letters, taken here from the mountain's name

parts.note: Skegness, a Lincolnshire seaside resort, was famously advertised as 'so bracing', meaning chilly and invigorating

explanation.surface: A mountaineer on Everest finds it as chilly as a windswept English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' takes M and E; 'when climbing' turns them to EM. Skegness is an English seaside town whose old railway poster said 'Skegness is so bracing'.
explanation.definitionFit: People hugging each other are holding together, joined as one.

clue.text: Shot has to drop into golf hole

indicators.note: into means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: the hole on a golf green is called the cup
to drop something, such as points or a game, is to lose it

explanation.surface: A golfer's shot has to drop into the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' is a golf stroke on the surface, but here a camera shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or photography shot taken from very near the subject.

clue.text: A male in jail turned up, given life

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the reversed word
in a down clue, turned up reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to jail someone is to detain them

explanation.surface: A man imprisoned shows up, having been handed a life sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes NIATED, and 'in' sets M inside it. 'given life' looks like a prison sentence but means brought to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something animated has been brought to life, as cartoon figures are made to move.

clue.text: Anything explained, head getting scratched

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and scratched means struck off

parts.note: a teacher who explained something taught it

explanation.surface: Anything explained leaves someone scratching their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head getting scratched' sounds like puzzlement but removes the first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for anything at all, as in 'for aught I know'.

clue.text: Song with new love brewing, I form pop group?

indicators.note: new signals that these letters take a fresh form

parts.note: bubbles are a group of things that pop

explanation.surface: A songwriter with a new romance stirring decides to start a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reworks LOVE BREWING I FORM into IMFOREVERBLOWING. 'pop group' looks like a band but is a cryptic description of bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A music-hall song from 1918, adopted as the anthem of West Ham United football fans.

clue.text: On rising I appreciate that weapon's loaded with nothing sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads everything from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: ta is a British informal thank-you

indicators.note: a gun loaded with something holds it inside

parts.note: a gun is a weapon; the 's stands for is
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: On getting up, someone grateful notes a gun loaded with no ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded with' makes GUON; 'On rising' turns the whole TAGUON upward. Ta is British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of nuts, honey and egg white, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Sitting on a seat that's empty to go

indicators.note: a word emptied of its contents keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: to ride is to travel, to go

explanation.surface: Sitting on a vacant chair, ready to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's empty' takes the outside letters of 'seat', ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with a leg on each side, as when mounted on a horse or bike.

clue.text: Puzzling question about right for sacred text

indicators.note: about means going round the abbreviation

parts.note: a koan is a paradoxical riddle used in Zen Buddhism

explanation.surface: A baffling question about what's right, posed in place of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy scripture of Islam, also spelt Qur'an.

clue.text: See 5
Maker of an instrument gripping end of cricket bat

indicators.note: gripping means holding the letter inside

parts.note: a fluter is one who makes or plays the flute

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An instrument maker holds a cricket bat by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of cricket' gives T. 'bat' is not the cricket bat but the verb, as in batting eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat eyelids is to flutter them, moving them quickly up and down.

clue.text: One is cracking

definitions.meaning: an ... in cards counts as one
cracking is British slang for excellent, first-rate

explanation.surface: A short statement that someone is splitting apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace is the card worth one, and also an informal word for excellent.

clue.text: Clash with Conservative entering amendment

indicators.note: entering means going inside the word

parts.note: an amendment is an alteration

explanation.surface: A Tory joins a parliamentary amendment, causing a political clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy argument or quarrel, a clash of views.

clue.text: Marvellous monkey revises, having failed

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An unimpressed tutor reports that a little rascal revises but fails anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having failed' reworks REVISES into RESSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressive inspires awe or admiration, so it is marvellous.

clue.text: Stuffed by white, black can suffer trauma

indicators.note: stuffed by means filled with, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: sable is the heraldic word for black
hock is a white German wine

explanation.surface: A chess or snooker scene: black, crowded in by white, is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' and 'black' look like chess pieces but are a white wine (hock, a German white) and the heraldic word for black; 'Stuffed by' puts one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily upset or startled is liable to be shaken by trauma.

clue.text: Money invested in raffle, paid back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
money invested in something is held inside it, so the letters sit within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cash put into a raffle has been paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left the hidden word unsignalled; 'invested in' is its indicator. FLEP sits across RAFFLE PAID and 'back' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging word for money or wealth, especially ill-gotten.

clue.text: Stuff coming up in strong suggestion of the future

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: forte means strong or loud, as in music

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to stuff, or fill, is to sate

explanation.surface: Stuff coming up powerfully hints at what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' gives ETAS, which 'in' places inside the word for strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample of something still to come.

clue.text: Baby boy, he plays with nun

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A little lad mucks about with a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' reworks BOY HE and NUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate names for a loved one, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Cut hydrogen by itself?

indicators.note: by in the sense of beside or next to, so the symbol is set alongside the first piece

parts.note: hydrogen itself is a gas
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about whether hydrogen should be cut alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' refers back to hydrogen, which is a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cut or wound in the skin.

clue.text: My work is going down at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: the setter's work is making the crossword, a compiler's composition

definitions.text: going down at the end of the day
definitions.meaning: the sun going down in the evening

explanation.surface: The setter complains that their work is in decline by evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter's job is setting the puzzle; the sun's evening descent is its setting.

clue.text: Pour liquid in to promote growth in bed

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the word

parts.note: to foster is to encourage growth or development

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, so the letters flow into another order

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: pour water into the flower bed to make things grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' makes URPO, which 'in' places inside. 'bed' looks like a garden bed but is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a tall post at each corner, often holding a canopy.

clue.text: Gymnast, one filled with spirit

definitions.meaning: an acrobat who performs somersaults and rolls
a drinking glass holding whisky or gin

explanation.surface: A spirited gymnast full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an acrobat who does rolls and a flat-bottomed glass for spirits.

clue.text: Break hearts in this way, splitting trousers

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter or letters

explanation.surface: Heartbreak like this, when your trousers split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts in' takes the middle of each of the four words; 'Break hearts' wants to be one phrase, but 'Break' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in continuity.

clue.text: Might one say, fat boy's first to tuck in to green vegetable? Out of the question!

parts.note: a jokey invented word: fat is not thin, so one might call it un-thin

indicators.note: to tuck in to something is to go inside it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: kale is a leafy green vegetable

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A greedy boy tucking into greens? Never going to happen!
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes B from 'boy's', and 'to tuck in to' puts it inside KALE. 'Might one say' flags the made-up word for fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so improbable that it cannot be considered is impossible to contemplate.

clue.text: Unqualified, say

definitions.meaning: to say a word is to speak it

explanation.surface: A curt note: someone lacking credentials, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means total, absolute; as a verb it means to speak.

clue.text: Tucker's best mate put on the covers of large sacred text

parts.note: the phrase 'best bib and tucker' means one's finest clothes, so bib pairs with tucker

indicators.note: the covers of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: An Australian's closest friend wraps a large holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best bib and tucker' is a phrase for one's smartest clothes. 'the covers of' takes L and E from large.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy scripture of Christianity, a sacred text.

clue.text: Force impacted

definitions.meaning: to have impacted something is to have struck or come into contact with it

explanation.surface: A police force hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met is London's police force; met also means came into contact with.

clue.text: Revolving part of a gun that's about to get two revolvers in one?

indicators.note: about means going around the second piece
revolving turns the word around so it reads backwards

parts.note: the butt is the stock end of a rifle
to win something is to get it

explanation.surface: A gun's revolving cylinder takes two revolvers in one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolving' makes TTUB, which 'that's about' wraps round the word for get. 'revolvers' are not pistols but spinning drums.
explanation.definitionFit: An old washing machine with two drums, one to wash and one to spin.

clue.text: See 5
Worker often seen wearing blue, red, green and russet, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or shady, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A list of colours, then a guess about a worker in blue uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reworks RED GREEN and RUSSET I together.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified hospital nurse, traditionally in a blue uniform.
